sentences.cn_text: 第一篇发表的素描作品《杨树步道的晚宴》让狄更斯在《每月杂志》的页面上发现它时热泪盈眶。
sentences.en_text: The first published sketch, “A Dinner at Poplar Walk” brought tears to Dickens’s eyes when he discovered it in the pages of The Monthly Magazine.

sentences.cn_text: 从那时起,他以笔名「博兹」在《晚间纪事报》上发表的素描作品为他赢得了一定的声誉。
sentences.en_text: From then on his sketches, which appeared under the pen name “Boz” in The Evening Chronicle, earned him a modest reputation.

sentences.cn_text: 《匹克威克外传》的巨大成功确立了狄更斯的声名。
sentences.en_text: The runaway success of The Pickwick Papers, as it is generally known today, secured Dickens’s fame.

sentences.cn_text: 市面上出现了匹克威克外套和匹克威克雪茄,那位体态丰腴、戴着眼镜的主人公塞缪尔·匹克威克成为了家喻户晓的人物。
sentences.en_text: There were Pickwick coats and Pickwick cigars, and the plump, spectacled hero, Samuel Pickwick, became a national figure.

sentences.cn_text: 《博兹札记》出版后不久,一家出版公司找到狄更斯,请他按月分期创作一个故事,作为当时著名画家罗伯特·西摩原创构思的系列木刻画的配文。
sentences.en_text: Soon after Sketches by Boz appeared, a publishing firm approached Dickens to write a story in monthly installments, as a backdrop for a series of woodcuts by the then-famous artist Robert Seymour, who had originated the idea for the story.

sentences.cn_text: 凭借一贯的自信,狄更斯成功坚持让西摩的画作转而为自己的故事配图。
sentences.en_text: With characteristic confidence, Dickens successfully insisted that Seymour’s pictures illustrate his own story instead.

sentences.cn_text: 第一期出版后,狄更斯致信这位画家,要求他修改一幅狄更斯认为不够忠实于自己文字的画作。
sentences.en_text: After the first installment, Dickens wrote to the artist and asked him to correct a drawing Dickens felt was not faithful enough to his prose.

sentences.cn_text: 西摩做出了修改,随后走进自家后院,以自杀方式表达了不满。
sentences.en_text: Seymour made the change, went into his backyard, and expressed his displeasure by committing suicide.

sentences.cn_text: 狄更斯和他的出版商只是换了一位新画家继续推进。
sentences.en_text: Dickens and his publishers simply pressed on with a new artist.

sentences.cn_text: 这部喜剧小说《匹克威克俱乐部遗稿》于1836年和1837年连载出版,并于1837年首次以单行本形式出版。
sentences.en_text: The comic novel, The Posthumous Papers of the Pickwick Club, appeared serially in 1836 and 1837, and was first published in book form in 1837.

sentences.cn_text: 查尔斯·狄更斯可能是19世纪最著名的英国小说家,也被许多人视为最伟大的英国小说家。
sentences.en_text: Charles Dickens is probably the best-known and, to many people, the greatest English novelist of the 19th century.

sentences.cn_text: 作为一位道德家、讽刺作家和社会改革家,狄更斯创作出复杂的情节和鲜明的人物,捕捉了英国社会的全貌。
sentences.en_text: A moralist, satirist, and social reformer, Dickens crafted complex plots and striking characters that capture the panorama of English society.

sentences.cn_text: 父亲出狱后不久,狄更斯在律师事务所找到了一份更好的工作,担任勤杂员。
sentences.en_text: Soon after his father’s release from prison, Dickens got a better job as errand boy in law offices.

sentences.cn_text: 他自学速记,以便日后获得更好的职位,担任法庭速记员和议会记者。
sentences.en_text: He taught himself shorthand to get an even better job later as a court stenographer and as a reporter in Parliament.

sentences.cn_text: 与此同时,狄更斯凭借记者般敏锐的观察力记录周围的生活,尤其是那些滑稽或古怪的事物,并向一些不知名的杂志投稿短篇素描。
sentences.en_text: At the same time, Dickens, who had a reporter’s eye for transcribing the life around him especially anything comic or odd, submitted short sketches to obscure magazines.

sentences.cn_text: 狄更斯出生于英格兰南部海岸的朴茨茅斯。
sentences.en_text: Dickens was born in Portsmouth, on England’s southern coast.

sentences.cn_text: 他的父亲是英国海军薪资办公室的一名职员——职位体面,但社会地位不高。
sentences.en_text: His father was a clerk in the British Navy Pay Office — a respectable position, but with little social status.

sentences.cn_text: 他的祖父母分别担任男管家和女管家,地位更低,曾是仆人,狄更斯后来隐瞒了他们的身份。
sentences.en_text: His paternal grandparents, a steward and a housekeeper, possessed even less status, having been servants, and Dickens later concealed their background.

sentences.cn_text: 据称狄更斯的母亲出身于一个更体面的家庭。
sentences.en_text: Dickens’s mother supposedly came from a more respectable family.

sentences.cn_text: 然而在狄更斯出生前两年,他的外祖父因偷窃被抓,逃往欧洲,再也没有回来。
sentences.en_text: Yet two years before Dickens’s birth, his mother’s father was caught stealing and fled to Europe, never to return.

sentences.cn_text: 家庭日益贫困迫使狄更斯12岁时辍学,到沃伦鞋油厂工作,那里的其他工人男孩嘲笑他是「小少爷」。他的父亲后来因债务入狱。
sentences.en_text: The family’s increasing poverty forced Dickens out of school at age 12 to work in Warren’s Blacking Warehouse, a shoe-polish factory, where the other working boys mocked him as “the young gentleman.” His father was then imprisoned for debt.

sentences.cn_text: 父亲入狱的屈辱以及在鞋油厂劳作的经历构成了狄更斯最深的创伤,成为他埋藏最深的秘密。
sentences.en_text: The humiliations of his father’s imprisonment and his labor in the blacking factory formed Dickens’s greatest wound and became his deepest secret.

sentences.cn_text: 他甚至无法向妻子倾诉这些秘密,尽管它们构成了他小说创作未曾公开的基础。
sentences.en_text: He could not confide them even to his wife, although they provide the unacknowledged foundation of his fiction.

sentences.cn_text: 《匹克威克外传》之后,狄更斯投入到一个更加阴暗的世界。
sentences.en_text: After Pickwick, Dickens plunged into a bleaker world.

sentences.cn_text: 在《雾都孤儿》中,他追溯了一个孤儿从济贫院到伦敦犯罪贫民窟的成长历程。
sentences.en_text: In Oliver Twist, he traces an orphan’s progress from the workhouse to the criminal slums of London.

sentences.cn_text: 他的下一部小说《尼古拉斯·尼克尔贝》将《雾都孤儿》的阴暗与《匹克威克外传》的明快结合在一起。
sentences.en_text: Nicholas Nickleby, his next novel, combines the darkness of Oliver Twist with the sunlight of Pickwick.

sentences.cn_text: 这些小说的流行巩固了狄更斯作为国内外公认的文坛巨匠的地位。
sentences.en_text: The popularity of these novels consolidated Dickens as a nationally and internationally celebrated man of letters.
